title: Beim Friseur und im Geschäft
summary: Handle service scenes with confidence — booking a haircut, browsing a shop, and the small-talk scripts that go with them

blocks.title: Service läuft auf Sie
blocks.body: In shops, salons and at counters, the register is **Sie** — both ways. The staff say *Sie* to you, and you say *Sie* back. At the **Friseur** (hairdresser) you'll book a *Termin*, then describe what you want. Keep it simple: nobody expects a speech, just clear wishes.
blocks.callout: *Ich hätte gern…* (Konjunktiv II) is your all-purpose polite „I'd like…” — from haircuts to bakeries.

blocks.title: Tap to hear the service phrases
Im Geschäft: die Kernsätze
blocks.body: In a shop the assistant opens with **Kann ich Ihnen helfen?** The magic reply for browsing in peace is **Ich schaue nur, danke.** When you're ready, you'll ask about size, colour and the fitting room — and finally whether they take card.

rows: Haben Sie das in Größe M?
Do you have this in size M?

blocks.callout: *Ich schaue nur, danke.* — say it with a smile and you'll be left to browse happily.

blocks.prompt: The assistant asks „Kann ich Ihnen helfen?” but you just want to browse. Best reply?
blocks.explain: *Nein danke, ich schaue nur.* — polite, friendly, and it buys you space to look around. *Ich nehme es* would mean you're buying on the spot.

blocks.prompt: Ask the shop politely: „Do you take card?”
blocks.hint: Sie-form of nehmen, inverted for the question.
blocks.explain: *Nehmen Sie Karte?* — the *Sie* comes right after the verb in a yes/no question. (*Kann ich mit Karte zahlen?* also works.)

lines.nl: Guten Tag, ich hätte gern einen Termin.
Nur schneiden, bitte. Nicht zu kurz.
lines.en: Just a cut, please. Not too short.
Do you have this in blue?

blocks.title: Sie im Service, du unter Freunden

pairs.left: Kann ich Ihnen helfen? — shop staff → you (Sie)
pairs.right: Kann ich dir helfen? — a friend → you (du)
pairs.note: In shops and salons it's *Sie* both directions. Save *dir* for friends. *helfen* takes the dative: *Ihnen* / *dir*.

blocks.scene: You run into Lena — you just got a haircut and did a bit of shopping.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.nl: Oh, neue Frisur! Steht dir gut. Warst du beim Friseur?
lines.en: Oh, new haircut! Suits you. Were you at the hairdresser's?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Ja, heute Morgen. Ich hab nur „nur schneiden, nicht zu kurz” gesagt — und es hat geklappt.
lines.en: Yes, this morning. I just said „just a cut, not too short” — and it worked.
lines.spotlight: *nur schneiden, nicht zu kurz* — the two phrases that get you a good haircut in German.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.nl: Sehr gut! Und die Tasche da, neu?
lines.en: Very good! And that bag, is it new?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Ja, im Geschäft nebenan. Die Verkäuferin war super nett.
lines.en: Yes, in the shop next door. The saleswoman was really nice.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.nl: Guck mal, dein Deutsch reicht jetzt sogar zum Shoppen. Stark.
lines.en: Look at that, your German is even good enough for shopping now. Strong.
lines.spotlight: *reicht zum…* — „is enough for…”. A nice way to praise progress.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Na ja, ich hab „ich schaue nur” gesagt und bin trotzdem mit einer Tasche rausgegangen.
lines.en: Well, I said „I'm just looking” and still walked out with a bag.

blocks.prompt: Play out a service scene: you go to the hairdresser or into a shop. Write what you say from start to finish — and use Sie throughout.
